concentration_time_figure.note: Total and free plasma concentrations reported separately, indicating substantial plasma protein binding.

notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 2.3 h is verified exactly against the Results text, for subcutaneous dosing. Note tmax is 4 h against a 2.3 h half-life, so this profile is absorption-rate-limited (flip-flop) and the value reflects depot release rather than clearance. The measurement is also strongly affected by plasma binding: total Cmax is 276 nM while FREE Cmax is 0.6 nM, a 460-fold difference, so what decays with a 2.3 h half-life is almost entirely albumin-bound material. As with PF1 in 27217590, PEPlife2 stores the sequence CYIQNCGKG - the same string it uses for PF1 - while the lipid moiety that drives the pharmacokinetics is absent; two different compounds from two different papers therefore share one representation while carrying half-lives of 2.3 h and 8.5 h. For context the paper notes native oxytocin's half-life is ~5 min and the related analogue ASK1476's is 3.2 h. No dose or group size is given in the body.
